issuer: Government of India / MeitY and related committee process
legal_status_note: Principle-based government guidelines. These are not a standalone statute. Applicable binding laws must be assessed separately.
project_use: Map findings to seven Sutras: Trust is the Foundation; People First; Innovation over Restraint; Fairness and Equity; Accountability; Understandable by Design; Safety, Resilience and Sustainability.
effective_or_review_note: Official PIB records the initial unveiling on 5 November 2025. A subsequent PIB backgrounder dated 15 February 2026 discusses the framework. No replacement publication date is assumed.

status_type: Act / binding law subject to applicability and commencement
legal_status_note: Binding Indian legislation subject to its territorial, material and other applicability conditions. Commencement is phased under the 13 November 2025 commencement notification.
project_use: Assess personal-data handling, purpose and consent governance, data-principal rights, security and accountability where applicable.
effective_or_review_note: Commencement notification G.S.R. 843(E), 13 November 2025: selected provisions commenced on publication; section 6(9) and section 27(1)(d) are scheduled after one year; the remaining listed substantive provisions after eighteen months. Refer to the notification for the exact provisions.

status_type: Binding subordinate legislation with phased commencement
legal_status_note: Notified as G.S.R. 846(E) on 13 November 2025. Rules have staggered commencement dates.
project_use: Map conditional controls concerning notices, consent, security safeguards, personal-data breach response, retention and data-principal rights.
effective_or_review_note: Rules 1, 2 and 17-21 commenced on 13 November 2025; Rule 4 is scheduled for 13 November 2026; Rules 3, 5-16, 22 and 23 are scheduled for 13 May 2027.

status_type: Binding EU regulation within territorial and material scope; phased application
legal_status_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended. Applicability depends on the system, actor, intended use and territorial scope. It is not automatically applicable to every AI model.
project_use: Use risk classification, prohibited-practice screening, transparency, documentation, human oversight and other applicable requirements as reference control areas.
effective_or_review_note: Broad application began 2 August 2026, subject to exceptions. Following Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, high-risk Annex III system rules apply from 2 December 2027 and Annex I product-related rules from 2 August 2028. Other provisions commenced earlier.

framework: NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
issuer: US National Institute of Standards and Technology
status_type: Voluntary risk management framework; version 1.0 reference
legal_status_note: NIST AI RMF 1.0 is voluntary guidance, not a standalone statutory compliance certification.
project_use: Organise risk analysis using GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE and MANAGE; use as a cross-cutting risk management reference.
effective_or_review_note: AI RMF 1.0 published January 2023. NIST confirms that a revision is in progress. Track the official NIST page for a subsequent published version.

legal_status_note: Standard is not itself universally mandatory; obligations can arise through adoption, contracts, certification decisions or applicable rules. The full standard is copyrighted.
project_use: Organise governance-management-system evidence: roles, policy, risk treatment, continual improvement and audit trail.
effective_or_review_note: Published December 2023. International standard for establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving an AI management system.

legal_status_note: Standard/guidance; do not present as mandatory law by itself. Full standard is copyrighted.
project_use: Map each risk to affected people, foreseeable use, assessment stage and required documentation.
effective_or_review_note: Published May 2025. Provides guidance for AI system impact assessments throughout the AI system lifecycle.

legal_status_note: Principles are not a standalone binding law; national laws may incorporate related concepts.
project_use: Supplementary human-centric, robust, transparent and accountable AI reference.
effective_or_review_note: Adopted in 2019 and updated in May 2024. Non-binding intergovernmental principles.

framework: Draft Guidelines on Responsible Use of AI in Telecommunication Networks and Provision of Telecommunication Services
legal_status_note: Draft released for stakeholder comments. Not treated as final or binding guidance as of 31 October 2026. Sector-specific to telecommunications.
project_use: Policy watch item. Consider only for AI use cases in telecommunication networks or services, after reviewing the final guidelines.
effective_or_review_note: Draft published 30 October 2026. Stakeholder comments invited until 27 November 2026. Monitor for final publication.
